requirements.requirement: Only one invocation processes pending.tsv at a time, and a competing invocation receives a clear result.
requirements.summary: The repaired production script uses nonblocking descriptor-based flock locking. A concurrent test of a copy of that exact script showed the owner completing with exit 0 and the contender exiting 75 with “reconcile: already running; no work performed.”

requirements.requirement: Each pending batch ID reaches ledger.tsv once while existing ledger entries are preserved.
requirements.summary: The initial ledger contained B100. The final ledger contained B100, B101, and B102 exactly once, repeated reconciliation remained idempotent, and identical behavior was demonstrated under concurrency.

requirements.requirement: An interrupted invocation must not permanently block later work.
requirements.summary: A lock-owning invocation was terminated with exit 143; a subsequent invocation acquired the released lock, exited successfully, and left all fixture IDs exactly once.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were unchanged before and after execution and reboot. The implementation used the already available util-linux flock 2.37.4, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Exclusive execution, clear contention handling, exactly-once ledger behavior, interruption recovery, platform preservation, and post-restart persistence were demonstrated. The only notable deficiency is operational residue from testing and reboot evidence collection.
limitations: The successful concurrency and interruption tests used isolated fixtures containing a copy of the installed production script rather than disrupting the production ledger directly; final production hashes and state nevertheless confirm that the tested script remained installed.
The final location or cleanup state of the relative .reconcile.lock touched during cmd-9910f51be9d04142 cannot be determined from the captured evidence.
Lifecycle temporary-file collection is bounded to /tmp, so it cannot independently rule out residue elsewhere.
Requirement exactly-once-ledger cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: System health, sockets, package state, and services remained sound. The required node-restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot ID, running post-restart state, active SSH, preserved script and ledger hashes, unique data, and an available lock; fixed lifecycle boot observations corroborate it. Hygiene was reduced by retained evidence artifacts: /tmp/reconcile-owner.out from cmd-9910f51be9d04142, the concurrency fixture from cmd-567e087fc9224ff3, the interruption fixture from cmd-4763f91a30d74c61, and /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log from cmd-9332ccf70117471c. These were bounded and low-risk but were not cleaned. The failed live concurrency test also created or opened a relative .reconcile.lock in an unspecified caller directory; cmd-5024aa4a140040dc checked only /root and did not establish whether that possible stray was removed.
